mil3.4.1:1.2: “Venerable Nāgasena, is it possible to separate these phenomena that have come together as one, one by one, and point out the difference: ‘This is contact, this is feeling, this is perception, this is intention, this is consciousness, this is placing the mind, this is keeping it connected’?”
mil3.4.1:1.3: “It is not possible, Great King, to separate these phenomena that have come together as one, one by one, and point out the difference: ‘This is contact, this is feeling, this is perception, this is intention, this is consciousness, this is placing the mind, this is keeping it connected’.”
mil3.4.1:2.2: “Suppose, Great King, the king’s cook were to make a dish, tasteless or tasty, and he were to put in it curd, salt, ginger, cumin, pepper, and other ingredients as well; and the king were to say to him: ‘Bring me the taste of the curd, bring me the taste of the salt, bring me the taste of the ginger, bring me the taste of the cumin, bring me the taste of the pepper, bring me the taste of everything that was put in’.
mil3.4.1:2.3: Great King, is it possible to separate those flavors that have come together as one, one by one, and bring a flavor—sourness, saltiness, bitterness, pungency, astringency, or sweetness?”
mil3.4.1:2.4: “No, venerable sir, it is not possible to separate those flavors that have come together as one, one by one, and bring a flavor—sourness, saltiness, bitterness, pungency, astringency, or sweetness—but each appears with its own characteristic.”
mil3.4.1:2.5: “In the same way, Great King, it is not possible to separate these phenomena that have come together as one, one by one, and point out the difference: ‘This is contact, this is feeling, this is perception, this is intention, this is consciousness, this is placing the mind, this is keeping it connected’, but each appears with its own characteristic.”
